extracted.intended_audience: writers, rhetoricians, and students of literature/classical rhetoric
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing 'the sublime' in writing: the five sources (great thoughts, passion, figures, noble diction, composition), what to avoid, how to recognize sublimity, and the innate + learned requirements for sublime authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great Thoughts (Grandeur of Conception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity to form noble, expansive ideas. The greatest writing flows from a great soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublimity begins in the quality and magnitude of the thinker’s conception — ideas should be elevated, large in scope, and worthy of sustained expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vehement and Inspired Passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong, authentic emotion that the writer feels and transmits. Passion that is felt becomes passion that is shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotion must be genuine and intense; affectation or manufactured feeling undermines sublimity. The writer’s own conviction energizes the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures of Thought and Speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Skillful, effective use of rhetorical devices — metaphor, hyperbole, asyndeton, polysyndeton, apostrophe — deployed to amplify, not decorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhetorical figures to intensify and clarify thought rather than ornament it; examples include metaphor and apostrophe. Balance and purpose are essential; devices should serve the idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noble Diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevated, dignified word choice. Vocabulary appropriate to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words of dignity and precision suitable to the subject; avoid trivial or incongruous vocabulary that diminishes grandeur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignified Word Arrangement (Composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The architecture of the sentence — rhythm, cadence, structural composition that gives weight to thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to sentence rhythm, cadence, and structural harmony so that form amplifies content; arrangement should confer gravity and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of True Sublimity
rubrics_metrics.description: The sublime 'leads listeners not to persuasion but to ecstasy.' It generates loss of rationality, alienation leading to identification with the creative process. The reader feels dismay mixed with exaltation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sublime passage aims to move beyond argument to an overwhelming aesthetic/spiritual effect; measure success by the intensity and transformative quality of audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Turgidity / Bombast (tumor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute grandiose, swollen phrasing for genuine grandeur; bombast is an anti-pattern that pretends sublimity through excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Puerility (meirakiōdes)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid small-minded cleverness or excessive polish that reduces weight; trivial finesse undermines greatness of conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid False Sentiment (parenthyrson)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotion in excess of what the situation warrants; misplaced passion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure emotions are appropriate to the subject and authentically felt; exaggerated or inappropriate sentiment breaks readers’ trust and deflates sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Frigidity (psychron)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strained conceits, far-fetched imagery that falls flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from strained or unnatural comparisons; imagery should illuminate, not alienate or puzzle the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing Sublimity — Bears repeated reading
rubrics_metrics.description: A passage is sublime if it bears repeated reading and yields more on each return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublime writing rewards rereading by revealing deeper layers, subtleties, and resonances rather than tiring or revealing only surface tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing Sublimity — Pleases all people at all times
rubrics_metrics.description: A sublime passage 'pleases all people at all times.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ideal suggests universality of effect: sublimity attains a kind of timeless and broadly human appeal (an aspirational test rather than literal expectation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing Sublimity — Strikes with thunderbolt force
rubrics_metrics.description: Sublimity 'strikes with thunderbolt force' rather than merely persuading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should astonish or overwhelm the reader with sudden, powerful impact, not rely solely on logical persuasion or slow accumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing Sublimity — Combines simplicity with magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines simplicity of statement with magnitude of conception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublime expression pairs clear, simple phrasing with grand, expansive ideas; avoid obscurity or needless complexity that masks scant thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Innate Aspiration / Great Soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Innate aspiration / great soul (cannot be taught).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longinus treats an underived greatness of spirit or taste as a prerequisite for genuine sublimity — a natural capacity that must underlie the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: Cultivated Rhetorical Skill
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical mastery of diction, figures, and composition is necessary and can be taught; practice and study refine the innate capacity into sublime expression.
